summary: Both prior refutations are fixed. The depcruise dispatch rejects --json before starting dependency-cruiser regardless of whether the flag is the positional token, before the module pattern, or after it, and missing flow/reaches patterns now return misuse with a specific diagnosis. The composite JSON test parser now throws on every nonblank stdout line outside a complete pretty-printed object, which covers prose before, between, and after values. No new correctness regression was found in the final AST JSON-output diff.

observations: The final production diff still routes all converted explanatory output through narrate(flags, text), which preserves human stdout and moves narration to warn/stderr only in JSON mode.
emit remains the single JSON result writer for registered AST verbs.
rot still has exactly five emit calls through its section loop; respell still has one exact emit and one conditional --near emit.
The depcruise refusal occurs before beginRun and runDepcruise, preventing a rejected JSON invocation from performing the expensive graph walk or emitting native text.
No new exit-code, truncation/meta, or stdout-channel regression was found.

limitations: Per instruction, the approximately 220-second full repository CLI suite was not rerun.
The focused test file exercises the composite parser and bounded production verbs; the eight depcruise refusal forms were verified directly at the Node CLI process boundary.

The documented pnpm wrapper itself writes an ELIFECYCLE line on stdout after any nonzero script exit. The underlying AST CLI produced zero stdout bytes in all refusal probes, matching the repository process-boundary tests; the wrapper behavior is external and pre-existing.
